title: The anti-neural role of BMP signaling is a consequence of its ancestral function in dorsoventral patterning
experiments_summary: The study employed multiple experimental approaches across several species. (1) Single-cell RNA-seq analysis: Published developmental single-cell atlas data from Nematostella vectensis were used to generate expression plots of BMP pathway genes (ligands, receptors, effectors, antagonists) across neuroglandular and retractor muscle cell subsets using Seurat. (2) Transgenic reporter line co-staining in Nematostella: Anti-pSMAD1/5 immunostaining was combined with multiple transgenic fluorescent reporter lines (myhc1::mCherry, soxB(2)::mOrange, elav1::mCherry, nanos1::mCherry, nanos2::mCherry, prdm14d::GFP) to determine overlap of BMP signaling activity with specific neuronal and muscle subpopulations in the retractor and parietal muscle regions of adult polyp mesenteries. (3) Immunostaining in medusozoan cnidarians: Anti-pSMAD1/5 co-staining with anti-α-Tubulin was performed in Tripedalia cystophora medusae; anti-pSMAD1/5 co-staining with anti-β-Tubulin, anti-FMRFamide, anti-serotonin, anti-GLWamide, and phalloidin was performed in Stomolophus sp. metaephyrae; pSMAD1/5 staining was also performed in Aurelia ephyrae. (4) BMP signaling inhibition and in situ hybridization in Nematostella: BMP2/4 morpholino (BMP2/4MO) and gdf5-like morpholino (gdf5-lMO) knockdowns were performed by injection into fertilized eggs. Chemical BMP inhibition using K02288 was applied across defined developmental windows (blastula to 2-day planula, 2-day to 4-day planula, 4-day to 5-day planula). Expression of neural markers (soxC, soxB(2), insm, prdm14d, pou4, elav1) was assessed by chromogenic in situ hybridization. (5) Bulk RNA-seq of BMP-inhibited adult Nematostella: Adult polyps were treated with 20 μM K02288 or DMSO for 5 hours, then dissected into head, body wall, female mesenteries, and male mesenteries. Poly-A enriched paired-end Illumina RNA-seq was performed in biological triplicates per tissue. Differential expression analysis used DESeq2. Resulting DEGs were cross-compared with published anti-pSMAD1/5 ChIP-seq data and BMP2/4MO RNA-seq data from early developmental stages. (6) Bulk RNA-seq of BMP-inhibited Stomolophus metaephyrae: Stomolophus metaephyrae were treated with K02288 or DMSO for 16 hours. RNA was extracted from four biological replicates, poly-A selected, and sequenced by paired-end Illumina. A de novo transcriptome was assembled with Trinity. Differential expression was assessed with Kallisto and DESeq2. Orthologous genes between Stomolophus and Nematostella were identified using OrthoFinder. Differentially expressed Stomolophus genes with Nematostella orthologs were then mapped onto Nematostella single-cell data to identify neuronal- and cnidocyte-specific gene expression changes. (7) BMP signaling analysis in Spadella cephaloptera: Anti-pSMAD1/5 immunostaining was performed across embryonic stages (early and late gastrula, early elongation, hatchling, early juvenile). HCR-FISH was used to detect bmp2/4 and chordin expression in gastrula-stage embryos. Staining was imaged by confocal microscopy.
